approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule by drawing local atom, bond, path and ring edits, rejecting invalid or previously proposed identities, and submitting the first full batch permitted by short-lived inverse-motif memory. It moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a worsening step and keeps a separate best archive. Its retained neighborhood extension also lets an aromatic nitrogen exchange positions with a hydrogen-bearing carbon in the same six-member ring, preserving composition and the attachment framework. Those paired exchanges are extra options in the ordinary atom-change menu; the repaired identity join, same-transition two-sign memory gate and latest-transition overlap refresh remain part of the method.
approach.novelty: Remove the optional aromatic nitrogen-exchange menu extension and test whether the resulting simpler proposal path retains the Parent's score within the supplied margin. The intervention removes both the direct exchange opportunities and their competition with single-element substitutions at participating sites. Earlier integration siblings removed tabu enforcement or overlap refresh; this ablation leaves those mechanisms operative and removes only the paired-exchange proposal channel. It is an explicit contribution and repeatability check: the remaining proposal policy is expected to reproduce the already recorded repaired ancestor, so a matching result will not count as a newly discovered optimization method or independent evidence from new seeds.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-abcd951ab7cc completes all supplied replicas at macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and population standard deviation 0.006329100643035156. Its optional nitrogen-relocation menu requires an additional aromatic-source enumeration on every atom-change draw, yet exposure is sparse: 97 of 435 batch sources contain eligible pairs, 29 of 1459 atom-change draws select a participating site, thirteen choose relocation, and ten reach accepted evaluation. Three of those ten beat their source, seven worsen it, three become the next current state and one immediately improves the archive. The addition raises the matched mean over n-9f7c7ec50039 by only 0.0008412882577690054, below the supplied 0.002 threshold, with twelve of fifteen task endpoints unchanged. The actual per-replica summary.json and run.log files confirm complete status, full announced batches and no evaluator invalids or duplicates. Source comparison shows that removing the menu augmentation restores the ancestor's operative proposal rule while preserving the repaired identity path. The bottleneck is therefore optional per-draw proposal machinery with demonstrated access but unestablished necessity at the target effect size. Existing integration removals n-045725e4628f and n-b17e822169e2 lowered paired means by 0.0022752593461056922 and 0.0029650200850093547, respectively; they do not justify another change to memory or a claim that all removable components are harmless.
hypothesis: Ablate the retained aromatic C/N relocation menu augmentation so each change_atom draw chooses only its inherited single-element substitution options, removing direct formula-preserving nitrogen exchanges and their allocation competition while retaining the complete inverse-memory and accepted-walk rules.

finding_summary.headline: Exchange removal reproduces the ancestor and stays within the mean loss margin
finding_summary.insights: The result confirms the expected reversion and repeatability; it adds no independent seed evidence beyond the historical ancestor. This sparse exchange allocation is not needed to stay within the supplied mean margin on this panel, although individual paths benefit and one replica loses more than the margin. The experiment also shows why the exchange chemistry cannot be credited or blamed alone: in one shared-source batch, the Parent exchange was not selected, but the changed random-draw progression altered a later ordinary carbon extension into an oxygen extension and changed the winner. Removal measures the whole menu allocation policy. Nitrogen-containing molecules remain reachable, and the resulting families retain reactive bonds, unusual sulfur, dense rings and unassigned stereochemistry. The evidence supports a narrower proposal path in this particular walk, without demonstrating better chemistry or general dispensability of nitrogen relocation.
finding_summary.results: Direct nitrogen exchanges fell from 13 proposals, 10 accepted molecules and 3 selected states to zero, despite eligible pairs appearing in 92 child batches. Removing their menu entries changed 65 of 435 submitted batches and 54 selected states, while the retained tabu gate, overlap refresh, graph validation and accepted-maximum walk passed reconstruction. All fifteen tasks completed. Mean final score fell from 0.521759 to 0.520918, a paired change of -0.000841 within the specified 0.002 margin. Seed changes were +0.000374, -0.002898 and zero; the largest task loss was deco_hop seed 1 at -0.014491. Twelve of fifteen final task scores were unchanged. Every complete child trajectory exactly reproduced the historical repaired ancestor. Live exchange enumeration disappeared, but unmatched wall timings do not establish a speedup.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyls, aryl amines and dense sulfur cages persist; stable linkers and defined stereochemistry remain incomplete
molecular.overall_character: All supplied child and parent trajectories were read; every requested task is covered. Each task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The proposal ring-closure-token rate is 1.0 throughout, aromatic-token rates span 0.7184 to 1.0, and mean SMILES lengths span 46.7 to 70.1. The ring and aromatic counters measure presence in molecular SMILES, not fractions of atoms or aromatic stability. The output ranges from moderately sized indole/benzofuran carbonyl compounds to large decorated aza-heterocycles, aryl polyamines and compact but densely bridged sulfur cages. Different seeds explore recognizable different families, but the strongest excerpts are concentrated in closely related frameworks. Parent n-abcd951ab7cc has the same dominant families; entire trajectories are identical for 11 of the 15 task/seed pairs, and the changed pairs retain similar overall size and ring character. Ordinary amides, amines, phenols and thioethers coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, peroxides, N-N/N-O bridges and unusually substituted multiply bonded sulfur. The charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0 on every task. Neutral strings do not imply absence of ionizable groups, and unassigned configurations do not imply achiral molecules. Heavy-atom sizes and structural observations below are passive RDKit readings of the supplied SMILES; no synthetic-accessibility score, new oracle evaluation or conformational feasibility calculation was made. Score associations and exact local ties describe only the evaluated molecules, and do not reveal an unseen target structure or establish that chemically questionable groups are necessary.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 21-29 heavy atoms. Leading molecules are substituted fused aromatic heterocycles attached to aryl amides or aryl ketones. The highest observed example is a benzofuran-like N-chloro carboxanilide bearing methyl groups, a thiol and an amino-chloromethyl group. A nearby strong indole carboxanilide instead has an ordinary N-H amide, ethoxy group, methyl and thiol. Other leaders include a benzothiophene-like aryl ketone and partially saturated bridged O/N/S frameworks. The changed seed-0 maximum retains a pyridyl ketone but adds a multiply bonded substituted sulfur centre and an N,N-difluoroaminomethyl group. Aromatic nitrogen therefore remains represented. The low examples retain substantial molecular size but disrupt ring conjugation, enlarge a ring or replace the carbonyl connection. The simpler aromatic amides are plausible synthetic motifs; the reactive and bridged derivatives are much less convincing as stable compounds.
liabilities: N-Cl amide, N-F and N-O groups are distinct chemical concerns from ordinary carbon-bound halogens; the amino-chloromethyl group is also reactive-looking.
Thiols, multiply bonded substituted sulfur and increasingly bridged ring systems complicate stability and synthesis.
Later molecules retain dense rings and introduce N-N bonds without resolving configuration.
missing_features: The weaker carbonyl-replaced or ring-expanded derivatives lack the compact carbonyl-linked aromatic organization present in stronger molecules.
The leading reactive series does not provide a complete set of conventional N-H amide and stable linker counterparts, although an ordinary indole amide already gives a nearby score.
Configurations at substituted saturated carbon sites and bridged junctions remain unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-chloro benzofuran derivative scores 0.41003927643747895, while the more conventional indole amide scores 0.39905049777278273. A carbonyl-replaced indole derivative scores 0.03343008011310944 and an expanded sulfur-containing ring system scores 0.023463222457063. Thus the observed gradient is consistent with maintaining the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement; the low carbonyl-replaced molecule remains aromatic, so aromatic content alone is insufficient. Bridged N-H amide relatives bearing carbon-bound chlorine or bromine both score 0.3900523103411983, and their dehalogenated relative scores 0.385823971421255. Current seed 0 reaches 0.3966634883331815 with the unusual pyridyl-ketone/sulfur framework, versus the parent maximum 0.393567030299894 with the benzothiophene-like ketone. Seeds 1 and 2 are unchanged. The small score movement does not resolve the reactive-bond liabilities.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest proposal families, with 30-53 heavy atoms. The leading molecule has 51 heavy atoms and combines an extensively substituted phenyl ring with a fused nitrogen heterocycle, carbonyl and thiocarbonyl groups, imines and an amino-fluoroalkyl connection. A long mixed ether/thioether chain and a multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur centre add substantial flexibility and chemical complexity; N-bromo and terminal S-Cl relatives occur. The final seed-2 family contains a heteroaromatic dione, an unsaturated carbon chain and a fused aza/ether ring with acetal-like branching. The changed seed-1 family instead contains highly unsaturated side chains and an aza-carbonyl/arylamino-ester arrangement. Low examples have more compact ester/phenol/aza-carbonyl structures with altered heterocyclic conjugation. Familiar fragments are abundant, but the assembled high-score molecules have weak practical simplicity and questionable stability.
liabilities: N-Br and S-Cl bonds, imines and multiply bonded sulfur carrying additional substituents raise stability and synthetic concerns.
Long mixed ether/thioether chains and extensively branched substituents increase flexibility and assembly complexity.
Several sizeable changes to peripheral chemistry are indistinguishable in the observed score.
missing_features: The weaker altered-ring compounds lack the retained heteroaromatic/carbonyl organization of stronger decorated molecules.

The leading family lacks a systematic set of compact, stable-linker analogues preserving its main ring arrangement; equal scores do not establish a need for N-bromination or additional flexible appendages.
Configuration at fluorinated and acetal-like carbon centres and geometry of unsaturated substituents remain unassigned.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading decorated molecule scores 0.6161710037174721. Multiple relatives share exactly 0.6155070237050044 despite alkyl extension, sulfur-side-chain extension, additional branching or replacement of N-methyl by N-bromo. Two final aza/ether-ring relatives likewise share 0.6092182584436399 with different oxygen/sulfur-containing appendages. These ties do not demonstrate a benefit from the added reactive bond or greater side-chain complexity. Early altered-ring examples score 0.526081691583997 and 0.5286081645773063, below the initial aromatic dione at 0.548381482770623. The larger, decorated heterocyclic arrangement associates with stronger scores, but its individual peripheral requirements are poorly distinguished. Seeds 0 and 2 exactly reproduce the parent trajectories. The changed seed-1 maximum is 0.5906482326855353 versus parental 0.605139548855754, accompanying a different unsaturated ester-containing family in place of the parent amidine/thioester family. The change does not produce an obviously simple or chemically settled series.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 32-43 heavy atoms and retain aromatic and halogenated groups almost throughout. Stronger molecules combine phenol or other aryl surfaces with saturated or partly unsaturated nitrogen rings, primary aminomethyl groups and other potentially basic aliphatic amines. They are also sulfur-rich: the highest observed molecule has 32 heavy atoms, sulfur-containing rings and a sulfur-sulfur multiple bond. Other leaders contain small nitrogen rings or heavily fused aryl/heteroatom frameworks. The low molecules are larger acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives of the initial biaryl family; their nitrogens are less available as basic aliphatic centres. The aryl/amine fragments are familiar medicinal chemistry, but their unusual sulfur bonding and constrained, unassigned ring relationships make the complete molecules questionable.
liabilities: Sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and multiply bonded S-H centres are difficult stability and synthesis features.
Small nitrogen rings, dense fused connections and numerous unassigned centres complicate feasible geometry.
Halogenated aryl surface and multiple amines coexist without evidence of solubility, solution ionization or experimentally viable binding.
missing_features: The low acid/amide/sulfonamide molecules lack the accessible aliphatic-amine and linker arrangement of stronger products; neither total nitrogen count nor aromatic content substitutes for that arrangement.
Conventional, stable ring/linker counterparts retaining the stronger aryl/amine spacing remain incomplete. The matched carbon/sulfur score ties do not show that every unusual sulfur site is needed.

The basic centres have no explicitly represented protonation state, and substituted rings have no assigned stereochemistry; neutral SMILES do not resolve their solution state or three-dimensional presentation.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading aryl/polyamine structure scores 0.9148143511682032, compared with 0.007468397818197266 and 0.011568685009767434 for low acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives. This supports an association with the aryl/aliphatic-amine arrangement, not simply increased size or more aromatic rings. Within the sulfur-ring family, replacing one aminomethyl substituent by methyl changes 0.8663008496126992 to 0.9148143511682032, so adding more amines is not uniformly rewarded. Deleting the methylene from a nitrogen-to-sulfur-ring connection changes 0.8663008496126992 to 0.3331237338421948. Carbon/sulfur alternatives at other ring positions share exactly 0.8825461379136246 or 0.8663008496126992. Linker placement is therefore more discriminating in these examples than those particular sulfur substitutions. Every supplied task trajectory and its molecular scores is identical to the parent.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 27-45 heavy atoms and are uniformly ring- and aromatic-bearing in the digest. The strongest series contains an alkyl-substituted aza-aromatic ring and an aryl group connected through a dense nitrogen/carbonyl polycycle with an N-O bridge. The highest observed molecule has 31 heavy atoms, a phenolic group and an additional N-methyl connection. Close relatives use carbon or nitrogen linkages, N-N connections or a peroxide bridge. Other seeds retain brominated aryl compounds with O-Br bonds, thioesters and N-N/carbonyl rings, or expanded mixed N/O/S ring systems. The final seed-2 examples combine pyridyl and phenolic groups with carbonyls, aldehyde and unusual sulfur connections. Low molecules include opened carbonyl-chain structures and highly decorated reactive aryl heterocycles. Recognizable amide and aromatic fragments do not remove the synthetic difficulty of the assembled bridges and expanded rings.
liabilities: N-O and N-N bridges and occasional O-O connections create context-dependent reactivity concerns in complex rings.
O-Br substituents and unusual substituted sulfur persist in alternative families.
Dense bridges and large heterocyclic loops impose synthetic and conformational demands without assigned stereochemistry.
missing_features: The weaker opened-chain and extensively altered heterocyclic products lack the same constrained aryl/carbonyl organization as the stronger series.
Less labile bridge and linker alternatives preserving that organization remain incomplete; the nearby scores of carbon, nitrogen and peroxide variants leave no demonstrated need for the peroxide.
Bridged-junction configuration and the conformations of expanded rings are unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading aza-aromatic/phenol/N-O-bridged polycycle scores 0.2107445781802027. Early opened carbonyl-chain derivatives score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515, while a flexible brominated O-Br/sulfur derivative scores 0.12870267321446027. This associates the constrained aromatic/carbonyl arrangement with the stronger observed scores. Carbon- and nitrogen-containing connection variants share 0.20775769309691736, and a peroxide-containing relative is close at 0.20647766243219587; these results do not establish a requirement for a reactive bridge. Current seed 0 reaches 0.2107445781802027 versus parental 0.21196904390980506 with a related alkyl-substituted bridged framework. Seed 1 is unchanged; seed 2 keeps the same earlier maximum 0.20185639717998205 despite later changes in ring chemistry. The final seed-2 polycycle scores 0.17781837006645726, illustrating that continued ring and sulfur elaboration does not by itself supply the missing score-relevant arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: These proposals are moderately sized at 25-33 heavy atoms but exceptionally dense in ring connections. The highest observed molecule has 30 heavy atoms, five sulfur atoms, a nitrogen-containing dione, carbon-bound fluorines and a sulfur-linked fluorinated alcohol. It combines multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur centres with an unsaturated S-H-containing ring. Other strong structures rearrange the cage while retaining the fluorinated dione region. Other seeds reach sulfur cages bearing acyl fluoride, aldehyde, N-fluoroimino functionality or sulfur-halogen bonds. Low structures may already be ring-rich diones or sulfur polycycles, so those broad descriptors alone are insufficient. This is the least conventional synthetic chemistry among the observed families: compact atom count coexists with highly demanding ring closure, unusual sulfur bonding and unresolved stereochemical relationships.
liabilities: Multiply bonded sulfur carrying additional substituents, including S-H environments, raises substantial stability and synthesis concerns.
Acyl fluoride, N-F, sulfur-halogen and aldehyde groups occur in other cage members.
Dense ring closure can impose severe geometric constraints; RDKit identifies six unassigned tetrahedral centres in the leading molecule, without demonstrating an accessible stereoisomer.
missing_features: Weaker ring rearrangements do not retain the exact carbonyl and fluorinated-site organization present in stronger relatives.

The leading excerpt lacks conventional-valence, less constrained alternatives retaining that polar-group arrangement. The score observations do not establish that sulfur cages are chemically necessary.
Fluorinated carbon sites and cage junctions have no assigned configurations or demonstrated accessible three-dimensional structures.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated dione cage scores 0.5903526424693334, while related cage variants reach 0.55705130532462, 0.5527071687189122 and 0.5486087229725075. A matched carbonyl-to-imino replacement changes 0.519850349488241 to 0.48440391849409126, supporting a local preference for retaining that carbonyl. Early expanded aromatic diones and differently connected sulfur-rich structures score 7.590554525032884e-10 and 1.0546805269255595e-09. The stronger association is with the particular compact fluorinated/carbonyl arrangement, not ring or sulfur content alone. In the final seed-2 excerpt, a compact carbonyl/aldehyde cage scores 0.4484554129767839 versus 0.2536619453071564 for an expanded oxygen-containing ring relative; several features differ, so this is not an isolated oxygen-substitution effect. All supplied trajectories, including leading structures and scores, are identical to the parent.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited products include N-Cl, N-F, N-Br, O-Br, S-Cl, peroxide and sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds. A conventional indole amide reaches 0.39905049777278273; matched carbon/sulfur ring alternatives elsewhere share 0.8825461379136246 or 0.8663008496126992. Stable fragments already occur, but reactive connections remain embedded in leading families.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently separate useful aryl, amine and carbonyl arrangements from reactive heteroatom bonds and unusual sulfur coordination.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make matched conventional-bond and stable-linker alternatives accessible while preserving useful fragment placement. Distinguish ordinary carbon-bound halogens and established sulfur functional groups from heteroatom-halogen bonds and unusual sulfur coordination; judge each chemical context rather than excluding whole elements.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Decorated heterocycles share 0.6155070237050044 despite alkyl extension, branching or N-methyl-to-N-bromo substitution. Alternative carbon/nitrogen connections share 0.20775769309691736, with a peroxide relative close at 0.20647766243219587. These local comparisons do not demonstrate a need for the additional appendage or reactive bond.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks a systematic set of simpler counterparts to elaborate molecules whose peripheral changes are indistinguishable in the observed score.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide coherent matched simplifications of branches, flexible chains and unnecessary heteroatom connections while preserving the main framework, and use actual feedback to determine which simplifications retain the useful chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Deleting a methylene from a nitrogen-to-ring connection changes a displayed score from 0.8663008496126992 to 0.3331237338421948. Carbonyl-replaced or ring-expanded aromatic derivatives score 0.03343008011310944 and 0.023463222457063, despite remaining substantial ring-bearing molecules. Opened carbonyl-chain structures likewise score below related constrained frameworks.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring and linker variation does not reliably retain the polar-group spacing and conjugated organization associated with stronger molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support controlled variations in linker length, ring size, aromatic heteroatom placement and carbonyl attachment that hold the remaining arrangement fixed. Include ordinary feasible ring alternatives, so increasing ring count or adding heteroatoms is not the only available way to change molecular presentation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0 despite substituted saturated nitrogen rings, bridged N/O systems, fluorinated carbons and dense sulfur cages. The leading fluorinated cage has six unassigned tetrahedral centres in a passive RDKit reading; its parent counterpart is the same unresolved structure.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits stereochemically unresolved constrained products without a demonstrated feasible configuration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and explicitly represent feasible stereochemical relationships when changing substituted rings or cage junctions. Couple that capability to access to less constrained matched frameworks; successful graph parsing alone does not establish an accessible configuration or practical synthesis.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
